drafted_from: tool row in tools/check-a-rendered-video/tool-rows.json, do-work/check_a_rendered_video.py and test/test_settings_row.py; the run was made on an ffmpeg test video with the test fixture limits; list:settings fields read from the account's list definition
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check my finished video /work/film.mp4 against my limits for the film sample-film and tell me every FAIL and WARN with the seconds it happens at." It reads your limits row from list:settings, writes it to a file and runs check_a_rendered_video.py check on your computer.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON. For tool:check-a-rendered-video the settings hold limits, the numbers and word lists each check uses, and the row id is record:setting:check-a-rendered-video~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>.

values.name: Limits for all of Sam's videos

instructions: 1. Pour the two example rows into your own settings list (see pour), or make list:settings from them, then fill in your own limits: the numbers and word lists each check uses. The tool has no defaults: a check with no limits says so instead of passing.

2. Say which video to check and which film or person the limits are for. The AI reads the row record:setting:check-a-rendered-video~film~<slug> from your records, writes it to a file, and reads the tool's row with tools:list {tool: tool:check-a-rendered-video}.

3. The AI runs `run` from the Workshop checkout: python3 tools/check-a-rendered-video/do-work/check_a_rendered_video.py check <video> --limits <file> --json <output>, adding --spec <file> when it has the JSON spec of the cuts and graphics.

4. Read the last line {"result": {verdict, videos: [{video, verdict, failed, warned, not_measured}]}} and the lines above it; for each FAIL and WARN say the check, the seconds it happens at and what it found, then which checks could not run (not_measured). Do not edit the video: say what to change.

worked_examples.title: Check a plain 3 second video against generated-video limits
worked_examples.ask: Check my finished video /work/film.mp4 against my limits and tell me every FAIL and WARN.
worked_examples.given: I ran the command on an ffmpeg test video (testsrc2, 320x180, 24 frames a second, 3 seconds, a 440 Hz tone) with the limits file the Workshop keeps for its generated-video tests, tools/check-a-rendered-video/test/fixtures/limits-for-generated-videos.json (see test/check-a-rendered-video.test.mjs). Command: python3 tools/check-a-rendered-video/do-work/check_a_rendered_video.py check /work/film.mp4 --limits /work/limits.json --json /work/findings.json. No spec was given, so checks that need cuts, graphics or an overlay report that they had nothing to look at.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"verdict": "PASS", "videos": [{"video": "/work/film.mp4", "verdict": "PASS", "failed": [], "warned": [], "not_measured": {}}]}} Above that line every check prints PASS with INFO lines such as "no overlay (a plain video, nothing laid over it): no overlay.mov" (settle, text-size, placement), "no added sound" (sound-sync, sound-loops) and "no hold, freeze or still of the person" (held-face); /work/findings.json holds every finding with its time.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
